standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the identification K tensor^L_B kappa(m_B) = (K tensor_A kappa(m_A)) tensor^L over B over m_A B kappa(m_B) and hence the degree estimate.

core_obligations: Use hypothesis (3) to replace K by a bounded above complex of finite free B-modules, so that ordinary tensor products compute the derived ones (proof lines 20247-20248).

Compute the derived fibre at the closed point of B: display the chain of equalities identifying K tensor^L_B kappa(m_B) with (K tensor_A kappa(m_A)) tensor^L over B over m_A B with kappa(m_B), and justify each equality, the second by basic properties of the tensor product and the third by the fact that K tensor_A kappa(m_A) is a bounded above complex of flat modules over B over m_A B (proof lines 20248-20262).

Apply hypothesis (4) to see that the cohomology of K tensor_A kappa(m_A) is concentrated in degrees a to b, and observe that B over m_A B is a regular local ring of dimension d, hence of finite global dimension d (proof lines 20262-20269).

Combine these two inputs through the spectral sequence of the tensor product of complexes to conclude that H^j(K tensor^L_B kappa(m_B)) vanishes for j outside [a - d, b], and finish by the fibrewise criterion for perfectness, which gives that K is perfect over B with tor amplitude in [a - d, b] (proof lines 20265-20272).
proof_roadmap: Replace K by a bounded above complex of finite free B-modules using pseudo-coherence (proof lines 20247-20248).

Write the derived fibre at the closed point as a derived tensor product of the fibre over A with the residue field of B over m_A B, justifying the three equalities of the display (proof lines 20248-20262).

Use the cohomology bound of hypothesis (4) together with the finite global dimension of the regular ring B over m_A B in the spectral sequence of the tensor product, to get the degree estimate (proof lines 20262-20271).
Apply the fibrewise criterion for perfectness to conclude perfectness and the shifted tor amplitude range (proof line 20272).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the local form of the perfectness criterion for a flat local ring homomorphism A -> B whose fibre B over m_A B is regular of dimension d, and it is content with a single cohomological input at the closed point of A, namely the vanishing of H^i(K tensor^L_A kappa(m_A)) outside [a, b] (statement lines 20228-20244). The proof replaces K by a bounded above complex of finite free modules, then computes the derived fibre at the closed point of B through the three equalities of the display, whose justification uses flatness of K over A and of the fibre over A over B over m_A B, and finally combines the cohomology bound with the finite global dimension of the regular fibre in the spectral sequence of the tensor product of complexes (proof lines 20247-20271). What makes the argument work is that everything is reduced to a single fibre, which is why only the closed point appears in the hypothesis.
